newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Iran criticises Israeli moves in Middle East.
newsitem.headline: Iran criticises Israeli moves in Middle East.

text.p: Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani said on Monday Israeli actions in the Middle East were turning so-called Arab moderates into revolutionaries.

"The minimum effect we could say this move had is that it is making (Palestinian President Yasser) Arafat and the Egyptians revolutionary again," Rafsanjani said of Israel's decision to press ahead with a new Jewish settlement in Arab east Jerusalem.

He told a news conference that remarks by Arafat and Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa at Sunday's Organisation of the Islamic Conference (OIC) summit in Islamabad could have been made by Khalid Islambuli, assassin of Egyptian president Anwar Sadat.

Arafat accused Israel of sabotaging the peace process by delaying implementation of agreements with the Palestinians. He also criticised the United States for vetoing a U.N. Security Council resolution demanding a halt to the Jerusalem settlement.
Rafsanjani said Iran had never believed Israel was serious about Middle East peace and its recent actions had shown the Moslem world that this view was correct.
"It has been quite clear for many, many years to us that from the beginning that Israel has never been interested in having peace," he said.

"And to me the face of (U.S. President Bill) Clinton sitting on a wheel chair with a broken leg vetoing the resolution on Palestine twice in one week is very similar to the face of (late Israeli defence minister) Moshe Dayan sitting on a tank with one eye shooting Palestinian people," Rafsanjani said.

"Should there be a reward one day to be given to any extremist group, then (Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu should be a nominee...because his hard line has definitely caused the Arabs and the Moslems an awakening.
"Therefore it could be understood that occasionally an extremist on the other side also could help the Islamic war."
